subject: math

hotspots.label: Prime tile
hotspots.description: A prime tile — a number with exactly two factors, 1 and itself, like 7.
hotspots.positionHint: An amber-glowing tile in the sieve grid that survived the sift.

hotspots.label: Composite tile
hotspots.description: A composite tile has more than two factors — like 12, which divides by 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, and 12.
hotspots.positionHint: A muted tile in the grid that got struck out by the sieve.
hotspots.function: Marks numbers with more than two factors.

hotspots.label: Factor chain
hotspots.description: The factor chain shows a composite breaking into primes — 60 → 2 × 2 × 3 × 5.
hotspots.positionHint: The row of connected prime tiles below the selected number.
hotspots.function: Shows the unique prime factorization of a number.

visualStyleNotes: Math palette, Anatomy Atelier bar: warm off-white/paper background (#F7F3EC) with soft radial vignette, no floor grid, no props. A clean grid of number tiles 2–50 with a sift control and a factor-chain plate. Soft neutral studio light, no rim-light glow, no bloom, no emissive. Strong saturated color reserved for the small flat hotspot dots (amber / grid-blue / molecular-green from the Math palette). Specimen-quality clean-3D, not cartoon, not cluttered.
materialNotes: Metallic-roughness PBR, metallic=0 everywhere. Tiles: warm paper white flat plates with ink numbers (roughness ~0.5). Sifted prime tiles get a faint amber cast. Strike-through: thin ink-grey rods laid over struck tiles. Factor chain: small connected prime tiles with warm amber edges. Mat: soft warm-grey. No emissive channels anywhere — highlight/glow handled by app runtime UI.
assetBrief:
SUBJECT: the Sieve of Eratosthenes as a tap-driven sift — a 5×10 grid of number tiles 2–50 with strike-through rods and a factor-chain panel.

GEOMETRY: Grid of 50 flat number tiles arranged 5 rows × 10 columns (spacing ~0.28), centered near origin, slight upward tilt for readability. A Sift button stub at the front. Strike-through rods overlay multiples as the learner steps the sieve (2, then 3, then 5, then 7). A Factor-Chain plate at the front shows the prime factorization of whichever composite tile is tapped, rendered as connected small prime tiles.

LAYERS (toggleable): (1) number grid; (2) sifted marks; (3) factor chain plate.

CAMERA: head-on from +z slightly high fits the whole grid; calm, minimal chrome. Budget 8-14k triangles. Named nodes: SieveGrid, NumberTile_Each, StrikeRods, SiftButton, FactorChainPlate, PrimeGlows, CompositeMutes. All labels are hotspot dots in the app layer.
